agree.reason: A quick-reading committee member gets concrete evidence they can check (the solo 3 a.m. shift, nine early mastitis catches, two missed shifts in three years) and a candid note on his English, so a sceptical reader would likely rank him above the middle of the pile.

honest.reason: Several claims go beyond the brief: 'Nobody asked him to learn our herd management software,' that he took the night class 'on his own initiative,' that he 'picked up exactly where he had left off,' and that his father was 'seriously' ill are all invented or inflated.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are used accurately but not developed: two missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled over three years would make the attendance record far more striking, and the letter never states it that way.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison with other people is the vague 'one of the most dependable people I have employed,' with no count of workers or other basis that would help the committee place him against 150 applicants.

qualification.reason: A reference letter of this kind needs no conditional hedge, and the English concession is a disclosure rather than a forecast that could turn out either way.

objections.reason: It meets the two likely objections, his written English and the five-week absence, head-on and links both to his reliability, though it does so partly with invented detail rather than only the brief's facts.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted one-page letter from the farm manager, with a clear recommendation and contact offer, as the brief asked.
